entries.label: The Mall core lawns and Capitol-Washington Monument vista
facts: The Mall extends about one mile west from the U.S. Capitol to the Washington Monument.
The core is bounded by Constitution Avenue to the north and Independence Avenue to the south.
Eight long lawn panels are separated by cross streets and framed by broad tree groves.
modeling_constraints: Preserve the uninterrupted Capitol-Washington Monument vista in baseline blockouts.
Do not compress cross-street rhythm until a gameplay traversal review documents the simplification.

entries.label: Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool and elm walks
facts: The Reflecting Pool maintains the physical and visual connection between the Lincoln Memorial and Washington Monument.
Elm-lined walks run along the north and south sides of the pool.
modeling_constraints: Treat the pool as an orientation landmark, not decorative water disconnected from the main axis.
Keep the north and south walks visually legible from gameplay camera height.

entries.label: Lincoln Memorial material and massing reference
facts: Upper exterior steps, Doric columns, facade and major exterior elements use Colorado Yule marble.
Lower steps and terrace walls use pink Milford, Massachusetts granite.
Interior walls and Ionic columns use Indiana limestone; other interior elements use distinct marble families.
modeling_constraints: Do not collapse all Lincoln Memorial stone into one generic white material.
Material variation must remain restrained enough to preserve the monument's large-value readability.

entries.label: Washington Monument material and silhouette reference
facts: The monument is constructed of white marble ashlar blocks backed by blue gneiss.
The obelisk stands 555 feet 5 1/8 inches high and terminates in an aluminum cap.
modeling_constraints: Protect the obelisk silhouette from nearby supernatural clutter at baseline world state.
Stone-tone differences may be represented only after reference-backed placement, not invented as random patch noise.

entries.label: Constitution Gardens organic landscape counterpoint
facts: Constitution Gardens uses grade changes, curving shoreline and an informal planted landscape rather than the Mall's rigid central geometry.
The Vietnam Veterans Memorial modified the west end of the landscape after the gardens were completed.
modeling_constraints: Preserve the visual contrast between this softer landscape and the formal Mall axis.
Do not flatten the entire zone into a level lawn during blockout.

entries.label: Vietnam Veterans Memorial wall material and orientation
art_use: orientation toward Lincoln Memorial and Washington Monument
facts: The central memorial uses polished black granite walls arranged in a broad V set into the earth.
One arm is directed toward the Lincoln Memorial and the other toward the Washington Monument.
The reflective finish is integral to the memorial's visual experience.
modeling_constraints: Treat the polished black granite as a distinct reflective material family, not generic dark stone.
Do not add decorative glow or surface noise that destroys the wall's reflective reading in the baseline world state.

entries.label: World War II Memorial stone, bronze and plaza hierarchy
facts: The memorial is predominantly granite and uses different named granites for vertical pillars, paving, plaza accents and pool coping.
Bronze elements are structurally and visually distinct from the stone architecture.
modeling_constraints: Use separate source materials for major granite roles rather than one plaza-wide stone shader.
Keep bronze accents readable without pushing them into exaggerated fantasy metallic color.

entries.label: World War II Memorial pillar and pavilion massing
facts: The memorial centers on an elliptical plaza and Rainbow Pool between the Washington Monument and Lincoln Memorial.
Fifty-six granite pillars encircle the plaza and two pavilions anchor opposite sides.
modeling_constraints: Preserve the 56-pillar rhythm and two-pavilion hierarchy before adding memorial detail.
Keep the memorial composition subordinate to the larger Washington Monument-Lincoln Memorial vista rather than blocking the axis.

entries.label: National Mall elm allees
facts: The Mall's central grass panels are flanked north and south by four rows each of American elm trees.
The cultural-landscape inventory describes almost six hundred elms, including historical trees and later replacements.
modeling_constraints: Preserve allee rhythm and canopy framing before adding high-frequency foliage detail.
Do not imply one genetically uniform tree asset; use controlled silhouette variation within the same family.

entries.label: U.S. Capitol Grounds east-anchor context
facts: The grounds immediately surrounding the Capitol cover 58.8 acres and are bounded by Constitution Avenue, Independence Avenue and First Streets east and west.
Curved walkways and park-like planting contrast with the Capitol building's straight neoclassical lines.
The grounds contain more than 100 varieties of trees and bushes.
modeling_constraints: Treat the Capitol grounds as an east orientation anchor and context boundary, not interchangeable Mall lawn.
Any playable simplification of the grounds boundary must be documented before detailed dressing.

entries.label: Smithsonian museum edge and north-south context
facts: Smithsonian's visitor map describes museums around the National Mall between 3rd and 15th Streets and between Constitution and Independence Avenues.
Ten Smithsonian museums are located along the National Mall.
modeling_constraints: This entry establishes occupancy/context only; each museum needs its own authoritative geometry/material reference before detailed modeling.
Do not infer facade detail or redistribution rights from the visitor map alone.

review_note: This ledger stores links and modeling facts only. No source images, scans, map tiles, measured drawings, or third-party media are copied into the repository.
